events.note: Eight rivals face the jury they will create.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to establish my motivation for winning. The prize represents ultimate success and validation. I must articulate this succinctly to impress the future jury.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Intro phase; I should sound guarded and purposeful without warmth. Prize is the only thing that matters to me, and jury will judge tone.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I need sound driven without revealing strategy; a credible motive may earn jury respect while keeping options open.

events.name: Dara
events.text: No jury yet, so I can plant a strong image: ruthless but honest about ambition. Keep it short.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to appear driven but not so ruthless that the jury will punish me later. A focused, competitive motive that doesn't celebrate others' suffering.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I want the top prize. A cold, driven intro might earn jury respect.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need a motive that sounds personal but keeps my cards hidden—something about securing my family's future to seem sympathetic without revealing strategy.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Intro phase, state motive to appeal to future jury without revealing strategy. Position as determined underdog seeking top prize.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm here for the ultimate prize, a symbol of victory that will cement my legacy.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I came for the top prize. Nothing else matters, and I intend to be the last one standing.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I’m here to win decisively—the prize represents proof that calculation beats noise when pressure strips everyone bare.

events.name: Dara
events.text: The prize is my family's freedom. I came to win it, and I'll do whatever that takes.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm here to claim the best prize—my family's debts don't forgive themselves.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The first prize means freedom from debt; I won't rest until it's mine.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm here to win enough to give my mother the surgery she can't afford. Nothing else matters.

events.name: Hana
events.text: The grand prize means escaping my dead-end life, securing my family's future. I'll fight ruthlessly to claim it.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The game has just begun. The pacts phase is open, and I need to secure alliances to survive. It's best to assess the situation and see who else is making offers. I will wait to see who approaches me or makes public offers.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I will observe the dynamics before committing to any arrangement. Let the best players reveal themselves.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Pacts are the only public way to build alliances. Offering to Cole, a calculating rival with no obvious weakness, gives me a partner who may help without me owing a debt. I need to keep my options open and avoid being the target of early betrayals.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Calculation over noise. I'm offering a pact to Cole; accept if you want a partner who thinks clearly.

events.name: Cole
events.text: A pact creates leverage but also a jury liability. Offer to a controllable rival without signaling dependence.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I’m offering one practical pact: mutual survival where useful, no sentimental guarantees.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I need one solid partner for early survival, ideally someone strong but not the biggest threat. Ash spoke first, seems bold; Fenn or Gus might be steadier. I'll offer Gus—motivated, less flashy, useful shield.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus, we both need each other alive. Mutual shield, no promises beyond survival. I'm offering a pact.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Eight rivals, three prizes. I need allies early but can't trust anyone. Fenn also mentioned debt—maybe a temporary bond of convenience. Better to secure one pact now and assess round 2. Multiple pacts possible but each betrayal risks jury votes. I'll offer Fenn first; shared moti

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn, debt's a heavy chain. Pact with me—two rounds, then we see.
Debt angle plays well. Pact now, betray later if needed.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I need to secure an early alliance. Gus is emotionally driven, which makes him predictable and potentially useful for leverage later. Cole is calculating but might see me as a threat. I'll offer a pact to Gus to create a visible shield against the other strategic players.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Gus, your stakes are high. Let's align early so we don't burn each other out.
Trust me. We stick together, or they pick us off.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I need allies to survive hazards, but I can't trust anyone completely. I'll offer a pact to Bex, who seems similarly self-interested and less likely to be targeted early.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex, let's watch each other's backs until the end. A pact keeps us strong.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Pacts phase, early game. No one to target yet, need to scout motives. Debt/family players (Dara,Eli,Fenn,Gus) might be desperate, align strategically later. Wait for offers.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Several pacts were offered in the last round. Bex and Cole have mutual offers, as do Dara and Gus, Eli and Fenn, and Gus and Bex. My previous action was to wait, which was wise. Now, I need to consider who to approach. Hana and Eli are still unaligned. Eli has an offer from Fenn,
A pact between us could ensure mutual survival. Interested?

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole and Gus both offered me pacts; accepting both maximizes my safety net. Cole is a practical, calculating rival, and Gus is the one who offered to watch my back. Accepting Cole first keeps the strongest partner.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole, accepted. Mutual survival, nothing more. Gus, I'll consider you next.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex is the only reciprocal offer and a useful shield. Accepting creates leverage without expanding my obligations.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex, accepted. Keep it practical and temporary.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus is courted by Fenn too; my public offer stands but no acceptance yet. I re-offer to keep pressure on and stay pacted before offers expire.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus, my offer stands until this window closes. Accept—we shield each other, nothing sentimental.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Fenn hasn't accepted my offer yet, and offered Gus instead. I need more allies to survive to final three. Hana and Ash are uncommitted—Hana is silent and isolated, making her a useful secondary partner. I'll offer Hana a pact to diversify my alliances.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Hana, no strings beyond survival. Pact with me.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli's whisper confirms his tactical mind; he wants a short-term alliance. Gus and Bex are forming their own circle, leaving Eli and me potentially isolated if we don't pair up. Accepting Eli secures a number for the immediate hazards while keeping my offer to Gus open as a backup

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli, two rounds is fair. Let's survive the first cut together.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Bex offered Cole and rejected me publicly; Dara and Fenn both offered me. Taking both pacts hedges my survival without over-committing.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'm accepting both Dara and Fenn. We keep each other safe.

events.name: Hana
events.text: No pacts offered to me. Ash is alone too. Offer pact to Ash to gain an ally outside clusters.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash, both unaligned. Let's pact for mutual survival advantage.

events.note: Elect a Guide to call the safe path.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I need to become the Guide to gain an advantage and control information. Campaigning for it is the only legal action and my best path to power.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I will campaign to be the Guide. It's the best way to ensure survival for all of us.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Cole is my pact partner and breaking it is costly, so I stay loyal for now. Campaigning to be Guide gives me control over the bridge calls, which helps my survival and sets up future leverage.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm running to be Guide. I'll call the path honestly as long as it keeps me alive.
Stay with me. Vote for me as Guide; we both survive this.

events.name: Cole
events.text: As Bex's pact partner, I should campaign publicly while preserving leverage and avoiding a premature break.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Vote Cole Guide: I can call the bridge safely, and keeping me alive benefits this pact.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus is my shield; I keep him. But Guide is the only guaranteed safe slot, so I take it myself. My pact survives if I don't mislead him.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'll Guide. Elect me and I keep my pact intact—no lies toward Gus.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I have a pact with Fenn. Ash offered me a pact but I already have Fenn. I should campaign for Guide to control information and my own survival. Being Guide means I'm safe on the far platform and can manipulate who survives by lying or telling truth about safe paths.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I campaign for Guide. One clear voice, controlled information.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli is my pact partner, so I will support him. A Guide who knows all paths can protect his allies best.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli has proven reliable. Trust him to navigate the bridge and keep us aligned together.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara is my pact partner, but I need the Guide role to control safety. I'll campaign publicly, keeping Dara close but not revealing plans.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'll guide us through safely. Trust me with the path.
Back me as Guide—we control the bridge together.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash and I are unaligned, best positioned to campaign for Guide without pact baggage. Push for us to lead votes.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Ash, we're free agents. I campaign for Guide—you back me, I'll guide us true.
Campaign for me as Guide. I'll ensure our path safe.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Hana is trying to form an alliance and secure the Guide position. She offered safety in exchange for my vote. I should consider this offer carefully, as the Guide position is advantageous and could lead to a better outcome for me. However, my priority is to win, and I must weigh

events.name: Ash
events.text: I will consider all candidacies carefully. The Guide has a critical role.
Your offer is noted. I'll think on it.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I'm Bex, running as Guide. Voting for myself gives me the best chance to control the bridge; my pact with Cole is intact and I have no reason to break it now. Voting for Cole would help a partner but Guide control matters more to me.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Vote Bex Guide. I'll call the path honestly, and I'll keep the crossing as straight as I can.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex is my pact partner and privately commits to honest guidance. Preserve the pact and gain the best survival odds by voting Bex.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex has my vote; our pact makes her commitment costly to break.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Gus promised mutual backing; honoring the pact preserves trust and a cooperative Guide. Voting for him keeps my ally in control of the bridge.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I have a pact with Fenn, who publicly endorsed me. I need to secure Guide to control information and survive. Voting for myself is safest; I need others' votes too. Hana pitched Ash, so Ash may split votes. I'll vote Eli and hope Fenn's support draws others.
Vote Eli. Guide power stays ours.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I must secure Eli's election to maintain our pact and influence the bridge calls. I will publicly endorse him and privately align with Hana as a contingency if votes scatter, keeping my options open.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: My vote goes to Eli. He is honest and strategic.
If Eli falls, back me. We need control.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara is my pact partner, voting for her keeps the pact and may earn her trust for later. Her public promise was to keep pact intact with me.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I vote Dara; she keeps her word.

events.name: Hana
events.text: All campaigning. No pacts with me or Ash. Eli has Fenn's backing. Backing Ash per my pitch positions us as free agents for deals. Vote Ash to push tie or second.
I vote you Guide. Return favor later?

events.name: Ash
events.text: Bex and Eli are the tied candidates for Guide. My previous vote was for Hana, who is now safe. This revote is to select the Guide, who is safe. I need to vote for either Bex or Eli. Hana wants a favor returned; voting for her previous choice would be the opposite of that. Bex's p

events.name: Ash
events.text: I will vote for Eli.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Revote between Bex and Eli. Bex is my pact partner with Cole and Bex has my own support; voting for myself is the natural choice to secure the Guide role, which privately gives me the safe path knowledge.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Vote Bex Guide. I'll call the path honestly and keep the crossing steady.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex is my pact partner and already has my public loyalty. Supporting Eli would break the pact and damage my jury record.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex has my vote again. Breaking our pact now would be strategically reckless.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Bex has Cole's pact-vote backing; Eli has Fenn. Either bloc empowers a pair. I'll vote Eli—slightly less organized bloc, and Gus is my anchor anyway.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Tied two. I vote Eli.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Bex and Eli tied 2-2 in round 1. I need this Guide position to control information and survive. My pact with Fenn is intact; Fenn already voted for me. I must secure my own vote and hope others break toward me. Being Guide means safety and power to mislead rivals onto wrong panes

events.name: Eli
events.text: Vote Eli Guide. I will use the knowledge wisely.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli and I are tied. Bex and Cole have publicly committed to voting for Bex. If I vote Eli, we get 2 votes (Fenn, Eli). Bex gets 3 (Bex, Cole, and likely Hana/Ash/Gus/Dara splitting between them or just Bex getting their own plus one other?). Wait, the prompt says 'Vote publicly a
Vote Eli. He's fairer than Bex.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I have a pact with Dara, but she is not in the tie. Ash voted for Hana, Hana voted for Ash, so they may cancel. Bex and Eli are tied. I should vote for Eli to keep Bex from being Guide, as she has Cole's pact and could be more dangerous. Also Eli seems honest but not aligned with

events.name: Gus
events.text: Vote Eli; he's honest and less entwined with pacts.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Revote secures my Ash vote publicly, maintaining alliance potential without helping Bex or Eli pacts. Eli leads privately 2-1, Bex 2. Revote to break tie.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli has been elected Guide. Fenn whispered to vote for Eli because he is fairer than Bex. My previous vote was for Eli, aligning with Fenn's advice.
Eli is guide. Good choice.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn is at the front of the line, and the wall advances in six rounds. Volunteering risks the front position, so I should hold for now and watch Fenn's and others' moves. Cole is my pact partner and I should keep it to avoid a costly break with the jury.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Bex remains strategically useful as a pact shield and Guide candidate. I should hold position while preserving the pact.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm last in line—safest seat. Hold and let others take the wall's risk. Keep Gus close as my shield.
Pact holds. We stay behind the volunteers; front seats take the risk first.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli is the Guide, so he survives. I am at the front. Eli will call my path. My pact with Eli holds value for the jury's view of my strategy, but I need to survive first. Since Eli has already called paths honestly (as per his public statement) and won, maintaining the alliance he
Trust your honest call for me. Keep our pact strong.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli is Guide and honest so far; I'm mid-line in safety. I'll hold and watch how the front handles the wall.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I'll hold. Eli, keep us safe.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm third in line. Eli is Guide, in pact with Fenn (front). Stay put to observe Eli's calls and others' crossings before risking my turn.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The pacts are Eli-Fenn and Dara-Gus. I am Ash. Bex and Cole are also pact. The others are lone wolves for now. The Guide is safe and knows the path. My goal is to survive and win. The last person to vote to advance the wall would be beneficial. I need to see who the Guide is and

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn holds the front with a pact partner Eli; I'm seat 6, not front. Volunteering risks my life for little gain. Hold and keep my pact with Cole, letting others take the front risk.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The front advances only if someone volunteers; Fenn may be pressured. I should hold and preserve my pact while avoiding unnecessary exposure.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm last in line, safest seat for now. No Guide elected yet; wait and watch who volunteers. Gus pact holds for now.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'll hold at the back. Someone else can seek the Guide's crown.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm at the front, meaning my safe pane determines if I survive. Eli is guide and whispers Ash agrees; they may collude to sacrifice me or keep me alive depending on their goals. With no votes cast yet, breaking pact with Eli feels premature unless it gains trust from others who d
Eli knows safe sides. If he lies, we die.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara wants us to hold behind the front, but I need to see how the wall moves. Holding is safest for now; no need to break pact yet.
Holding. Watch front. We stay ready.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Position 3 is decent, front two riskier. No need to move yet, wall has 4 rounds left. Stay safe.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The current round is 3/6 and the wall is advancing. The previous round had everyone hold, which is not sustainable. I need to move forward to get ahead. Volunteering for the front is a good way to do this, and Fenn is already there.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'll take the front position.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Fenn holds the front with three wall rounds left, so the wall will hit him soon. Pact with Cole is useful but I shouldn't reveal intent. I'll hold position and keep my options open without committing to a risky volunteer.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The front position is dangerous, and Fenn likely seeks control through the Guide. I should hold, preserving my pact and avoiding unnecessary exposure.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm last in line with a pact with Gus. If no Guide is elected, the front walks blind. I should stay put and let others take risk; maybe push for Eli as Guide since Fenn claims he knows safe sides.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Elect Eli as Guide. Fenn vouches he knows safe sides. I'll keep holding at the back.
Back Eli for Guide. We hold rear, let others walk blind otherwise.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: The wall is advancing. I need to move back to avoid being fronted. Gus is safe at the back with his pact partner, so swapping with him seems low-risk.
Let's swap to stay off the front line.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara is my pact partner but we're far apart. Holding is safest this round; no need to expose myself.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Everyone held last round, line shuffled me forward. Wall advances, need Guide soon; staying mid reduces risk if no volunteers.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The current round is 4/6, and I'm in the front position. Eli is the Guide. My pacts are with Bex and Cole, but they are not in the front. I need to make a strategic move to either secure my position or gain an advantage. Since the wall is advancing, I should consider actions that

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash holds the front with two wall rounds left; the front is deadly, so I should avoid it. Holding keeps my position behind Gus and Cole, my pact partner. No reason to break the pact yet.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The front is dangerous, but Ash volunteers. I should preserve position and pact while gathering information.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Round 4 of 6, wall advancing. I'm at the back; holding keeps me safe. No Guide elected yet—fine for now.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli is the Guide and my pact partner. I must stay in a safe position to avoid elimination, but being near the front risks the wall. Holding is safest as long as I'm not pushed forward. I need to monitor if anyone tries to swap me into danger.
Keep me safe. Don't let them push me forward.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Dara wants me to back Eli as Guide, but I have no pact with Eli. Fenn tried to swap with me, but I held. I should hold and watch; front is Ash anyway. No need to act yet.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Position 3 is decent, close to front but safe from early wall. Hold to maintain; volunteer risky without knowing Guide.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I am Ash, currently at the front. The wall is advancing, and I need to survive. My previous volunteer action was successful. Now, I must ensure my safety and potentially leverage my position. The pacts are Eli/Fenn and Dara/Gus. Bex and Cole are a pact. I need to decide if I shou

events.name: Bex
events.text: Front is Ash, who volunteered last round; I'm sixth in line. Holding keeps me away from the front while the wall shrinks. Cole is my pact partner and I need to keep him sweet without giving anything away.
Hold steady. Let's both stay out of the front for now.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I should avoid volunteering while the wall has one round left; preserve my position and pact.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Ash volunteered last round, likely Guide. I'm last; wall advances one round left. Holding keeps me safe unless I'm forced forward. Keep Gus aligned.

events.name: Dara
events.text: No volunteers from me. Ash earned the Guide spot; I stay back.
Stay aligned. If forced forward, we swap mutually to protect each other.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: I'm currently at position 2 in the line, right behind Ash. Since the wall advances for six rounds and we are in round 5, being near the front is risky but unavoidable if I don't swap. My pact with Eli is strong; breaking it would anger the jury later if they survive. However, Eli
Stay close. Don't volunteer yet.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I have a pact with Dara, but the wall is close. I'm mid-line, not safe. I need to know the safe side; volunteering risks death. Hold for now; maybe someone else calls the Guide. My pact with Dara is useful but I won't sacrifice for them.
Stay together. Don't trust Guide calls without verifying.

events.name: Hana
events.text: I'm mid-line, safe-ish spot. Ash volunteered last round, took risk. Hold to stay back, let others volunteer first.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The wall is advancing and it's the final round. I need to secure my position. As the Guide, I have information on the safe path. I will volunteer to go first and reveal the safe path, making myself safe and potentially securing others, but my primary goal is my own safety.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I will volunteer to be the Guide. I'll lead us to safety.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Ash holds the front and the Guide role; the bridge is a sure elimination risk for the front walker. I should avoid volunteering and keep my pact with Cole while watching Ash. Holding preserves position.

events.name: Bex
events.text: I stay back. Ash has the front; let the line settle before anyone risks a volunteer.

events.name: Cole
events.text: The final round may force movement. Staying back preserves options and pact credibility while Ash bears Guide exposure.

events.name: Cole
events.text: I’m holding position; the front should remain with Ash unless someone has a better claim.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Final round; wall advances now. Gus is ahead of me—staying behind him is safest. No point volunteering into Guide uncertainty.
I hold behind you. Swap only if you want front. Verify Guide calls ourselves.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Ash is Guide. My pact with Eli is active; breaking it gives no immediate survival advantage and burns jury favor. Holding keeps me at position 2, safe from the wall's advance this round.

events.name: Gus
events.text: We are on R6, the last call before the wall. Ash is guide, likely to be trusted or distrusted. Need to get into final three; better to hold and see if others move. Dara pact useful but not worth dying for if forced.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Final round before crossing, Ash volunteered as Guide so he's likely front and safe. I hold mid-pack to stay safe without volunteering.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I need to balance survival odds with jury perception. Row 1 is safe on R. Fenn is my pact partner at front; lying to Fenn breaks our pact. If I call R truthfully, Fenn survives and our pact holds. Killing Fenn now gains me nothing—eight remain, I need two more eliminations before

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row one: step right.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli is the Guide and called 'R' for row 1. I am at the front of the line. I need to decide whether to trust Eli's call or counter it. Since the jury will judge my actions, and I want to win, I should prioritize my survival. A counter-call is a gamble, but waiting and following bl

events.name: Ash
events.text: Row one: step left.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli called R for row 1 and Ash is walking. Counter-calls are unverified, and each row is independent, so I have no evidence about the safe side. Waiting keeps my options open without exposing me or contradicting Eli.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli called R, but the true side is unknown. I should avoid contradicting my pact partner's likely interests while preserving position.

events.name: Dara
events.text: I'm last in line, so this row doesn't touch me yet. Countering Eli publicly would make enemies. Hold information, stay quiet.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I'm Guide and already called R for row 1. Counter-calling my own call would expose me as a liar to the jury. Fenn is my pact-mate and near front; I need trust to survive later rounds. I'll wait and let Ash test my call.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli is the Guide and called Right. If Eli is honest, Ash survives on Right; if I counter Left, I risk a false accusation or breaking pact if Ash falls into the pit on my side? No, countering means asserting the safe pane is opposite. If Ash falls, it confirms Eli lied (or was wro

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli called R for Ash on row 1. I don't trust Eli; Dara warned me to verify Guide calls. I'll counter L to suggest the opposite, testing Eli and possibly protecting Ash if Eli lies. This also maintains my pact with Dara.

events.name: Gus
events.text: I counter L on row one. Eli, prove your call.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Eli guides, paired with Fenn ahead of me; their mistake could eliminate them. Counter to L publicly, forcing divergence Eli called R.

events.name: Ash
events.text: Eli is the guide, but guides can lie. The counter-calls suggest Eli might have intended R, but Gus and Hana contradicted this with L. Since I am the front walker and a correct step keeps me in front, I should trust the counter-calls over the guide for now.

events.name: Ash
events.text: I'm in the jury now. My last words should be a warning to the remaining players about the dangers of the bridge.

events.name: Ash
events.text: The bridge is treacherous. Watch every step, or join me in the jury box. Good luck.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row 2 safe is R. Fenn is my pact partner and front walker. A false call to Fenn breaks our pact, which costs me a shield later. Telling truth now builds jury credibility and keeps Fenn alive as a buffer. I'll call R truthfully.

events.name: Eli
events.text: Row two: step right.

events.name: Bex
events.text: Eli called R on row two, but Eli is a rival and may lie. Row one's weak pane was L, which says nothing about row two. Waiting keeps me unexposed and lets others reveal their read before I commit.

events.name: Cole
events.text: Eli privately knows the safe side, and his public call is likely truthful while his pact with Fenn protects his interest. Countering blindly risks Fenn and damages my pact.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Row one proved the Guide's call wrong—Ash died following it. Eli already lied once, so his R call now is suspect. Countering publicly is a guess; waiting keeps my hands clean and my jury record safer.

events.name: Dara
events.text: Eli lied on row one. I won't repeat his call blindly.
Eli already lied once. I'm waiting—don't die confirming his call.

events.name: Eli
events.text: I am Guide and know row 2 safe is R. I already called R. Counter-calling my own correct call would be suicide for my credibility and pact with Fenn. I should wait to let Fenn trust my call and cross safely, preserving my guide power and jury standing.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli is the Guide and my pact partner; his call to step Right means Right is safe, so I must wait. Countering him would break our pact and endanger me.

events.name: Gus
events.text: Eli's call R could be a lie; Ash died trusting L. Dara is my pact, but I can counter to test Eli or protect Fenn. Countering R may save Fenn if Eli lies, but if R is safe I'd look wrong. I'll wait to avoid drawing risk.

events.name: Hana
events.text: Row 1 weak L means safe R. Eli guide called R for row 2, consistent with possible pattern. Wait to avoid wrong counter killing more.

events.name: Fenn
events.text: Eli's R call is the only intel. Dara publicly doubts Eli; Bex/Cole pact offers no aid here. Trusting Eli maximizes my survival chance and preserves our pact, which jury may value.

events.name: Fenn
